linh_nguyen.md:
- The nine duties listed in the posting appear as the nine bullets of the candidate's current job, in the same order and nearly the same words
- The employers are described only as "Leading Fintech Company" and "Global Technology Solutions Firm", with no names, team sizes, numbers or incidents
- Phone screen: ask about one specific Kubernetes upgrade they ran and what went wrong
review: yes
soojin_kim.md:
- The resume's qualifications section repeats the posting's requirements list word for word, bullet by bullet
- The current job is described as "You will design, build and operate...", which is how a posting talks to an applicant, not how a person describes their own work
- Employers are given only as "Fintech Startup" and "Technology Company"
review: yes
petr_ivanov.md:
- The opening "Mission" paragraph is the posting's description of the role, reworded into the first person
- The qualifications summary walks through every posting requirement in the posting's order as one long paragraph
- The two earlier jobs are a single line each, with unnamed employers
review: yes
jordan_harris.md:
- Each posting duty appears as a resume bullet with a word swapped ("Design, build and operate" becomes "Architected and operated"), keeping the same nine-bullet order
- Employers are given as "Confidential Financial Services Company", "Enterprise Software Organization" and "Technology Consultancy"; there are no numbers anywhere
- Phone screen: ask which company it was and how much transaction volume it handled
review: yes
arjun_singh.md:
- The bullets follow the posting's order and wording, with a percentage added to the end of each one
- Every percentage is a round number (80%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 90%, 100%, 300%) and every uptime figure is 99.99%
- Employers and dates are real-looking, but no number is tied to a specific system, incident or time period
- Phone screen: pick two of the percentages and ask how they were measured
review: yes
marcus_chen.docx:
- Flagged only because most of the posting's acronyms appear; the wording is the candidate's own and mentions tools the posting never does
- Plenty of concrete detail: 14 AWS accounts, about $2B in payment volume, a 31% cost reduction with the specific steps that got there
- Nothing suggests the wording came from the posting
review: no
